title: Gmail's Live AI search feature arrives for Google AI subscribers
key_facts: Gmail Live is out of beta after being announced at Google I/O, for Google AI plan subscribers.
It lets users search their inbox with conversational voice commands, similar to live voice chats with the Gemini chatbot but customised for Gmail, Docs and Drive.
Google's example questions: 'What's my flight's gate number?' and 'What's going on at my kid's school this week?'
Docs Live lets users tell Gemini what document they want and pulls details from Gmail, Drive, Chat and the web to build a first draft.
Keep Live turns spoken 'brain dumps' into organised notes and lists.
Features roll out this week in Gmail and Keep for Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers; Docs is limited to Pro and Ultra subscribers.
All of the features are 'coming soon' for Google Workspace business customers.
quote_evidence: Now out of beta after being announced at Google I/O last month, the AI feature allows you to search your inbox using conversational voice commands.
The new features are rolling out this week in Gmail and Keep, but only for Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers, with Docs limited to Pro and Ultra subscribers.
All of the features are also "coming soon" for Google Workspace business customers.
why_it_matters_hint: Google's voice AI now reads a subscriber's inbox and documents to answer questions, a paid-tier feature.
event_date: rolling out the week of 12 Oct 2026; Engadget article 16 Oct 2026
notes: Engadget says the I/O announcement was 'last month'; the summary does not repeat that timing.
